summary: A clever, fairly quick city-building game where players lay tiles onto a shared, ever-growing city, stacking new buildings on top of old ones to reshape the skyline. Each player also manages a personal hand of resource and role cards that convert into points, resources, or new tiles.
praised: elegant tile-stacking mechanism that keeps the city evolving
quick, tight playtime for the depth offered
scales well across player counts including solo
criticised: can feel like multiplayer solitaire with limited direct conflict
thin sci-fi theme that many find pasted-on
card draw luck in what resources/roles are available
some find the scoring a bit abstract or hard to track

interaction.kind: shared city board with tile stacking and district takeover
interaction.detail: Players build directly onto a single shared city map, and placing a new tile can bury or extend a rival's district, changing who benefits from its output. Alongside that shared board, each player keeps a private hand of resource, building, and role cards that they manage largely on their own.

subsystems: city tile stacking and card-hand building (one integrated engine)
sources: VP from exposed building tiles you control
VP from color-set bonuses among cards in hand
scoring.how_you_win: Place and stack district tiles to expose your own buildings and collect matching card sets; when the tile supply runs out, the player with the most VP from exposed tiles and card sets wins.
